noAreaKey: You don't have this area's key — you can't save here.

claim.asksHost: asks the host for a place

appointmentOptions.none: — you don't write in any calendar —

linkCalendar.title: Calendar
linkCalendar.opened: Opened from a link, without an account — {access}.
linkCalendar.mayWrite: You can add and change appointments here.
linkCalendar.signIn: Have an account? Sign in to see your own calendar.

people.empty: There are no other people in this group yet.

pick.unknown: Right now it says “{value}” — that is not the calendar of any of your groups. Choose the right one.
pick.noCalendars: You don't have any group calendar yet.
pick.goneOne: One of the chosen calendars is no longer available — tick the right ones.
pick.pageNote: On the page everyone sees the appointments they may see. In full screen, the people running the calendar can also add and change appointments.
pick.noItems: This calendar has no appointments in the coming year.
pick.itemGone: The chosen appointment doesn't belong to this calendar (or is long past) — choose another.
pick.partsHint: You add programme items in the calendar: open the appointment and “Add programme item”.

part.noCalendar: Appointments will appear here — a calendar still needs to be chosen.
part.joinNamed: Link “{label}” in this browser lets you add appointments here ({access}). You are signed in — add it to your account and you will write as yourself.
part.join: A link in this browser lets you add appointments here ({access}). You are signed in — add it to your account and you will write as yourself.

settings.title: Calendar settings
settings.intro: Calendar settings are the defaults for every new appointment — a single appointment can change them later.
settings.description: How appointments work in this calendar
settings.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. The talk takes 40 minutes. Come 5 minutes early. The confirmation comes from the office.
settings.descriptionHint: Everyone who sees the calendar will see this description.
settings.ownerLong: Who runs it (adds and changes appointments)
settings.massHint: Intentions are taken at the mass — in the calendar or in “Masses and services”. You enter who celebrates at the appointment.
settings.reserveAnyone: anyone who finds the appointment (e.g. on a page)
settings.reserveAnyoneHint: or only people of the chosen group (and the groups below it)
settings.reserveHint: E.g. confirmation candidates: only people of this group — including those with a personal link.
settings.archiveAsk: Archive this calendar? Its appointments will disappear from view but will not be deleted.

taskDay.title: Tasks · {date}
taskDay.empty: There are no tasks on this day.

more.one: And {count} more older overdue task — it will show here once these are done or skipped.
more.other: And {count} more older overdue tasks — they will show here once these are done or skipped.

tasks.noKey: Without a key in this tab, tasks are locked — sign in again or unlock the key.
tasks.empty: You don't have any tasks yet. A task has its own time (e.g. a prayer at 21:00 every day) or comes back some time after it was done (e.g. water the flowers every 3 days).
tasks.allDueAbove: All of them are due now — see above.

window.label: At a set time
window.says: Has its own time, which may repeat — e.g. a prayer at 21:00 every day. You tick off each occurrence; missed ones show.

period.label: For a while, regularly
period.says: Has time to get done and comes back every so often — e.g. cleaning the church: 3 days to do it, every 2 weeks. It appears at the start and grows more urgent until the end.

after.label: Every so often after doing it
after.says: Counts the time since it was last done — e.g. water the flowers every 3 days. When you tick it off, the counter starts again.

taskDialog.endBeforeStart: The end falls before the start.
taskDialog.windowTooLong: A window longer than a year — that is a resolution, not an appointment.
taskDialog.tooOften: The task can't come back more often than it lasts — lengthen the interval or shorten the time to do it.
taskDialog.periodTooLong: Time to do it longer than a year — that is a resolution, not a task.
taskDialog.fromChat: From a chat — the task will remember which message it came from and show up next to it.
taskDialog.afterHint: First time: {first} — then {every} after each time it is done.
taskDialog.remindHint: The reminder arrives on the devices where you have notifications turned on.
taskDialog.deleteAsk: Delete this task? Its history stays in the archive.

details.endAfterStart: The end must be after the start.
details.ownClaimConfirmed: This is your booking (confirmed). You change it where you made it.
details.ownClaimWaiting: This is your booking (awaiting confirmation). You change it where you made it.
details.readOnly: You can only view this appointment — you don't write in its calendar.

pickBar.skippedAllDay: All-day ones move only by whole days — unchanged: {terms}.
pickBar.removeAskSeries: Delete {terms}? From series, only these days will disappear.
pickBar.endAsk: End {series} before the selected day? Earlier appointments stay, single appointments disappear.
pickBar.ended: Done — the series end before the selected days.
pickBar.removeSeriesAsk: Delete {series} entirely — including appointments that already took place?
pickBar.label: Selected appointments
pickBar.cutHint: Ctrl + X — then click a day or an hour
pickBar.copyHint: Ctrl + C — then click a day or an hour
pickBar.endFollowing: These and the following — end the series
pickBar.allDayOnly: All-day ones move only by whole days.
pickBar.clipCut: To move: {terms} — click the day or hour where they should go
pickBar.clipCopy: To copy: {terms} — click the day or hour where they should go

editor.needsWhen: Enter the day and the hours.
editor.partsFailed: Appointment saved, but {failed} of {total} programme items could not be changed along with it.
editor.endAsk: End the series before this day? Earlier appointments stay.
editor.followingNote: From this day on — earlier appointments stay as they were. Intentions, assignments and sign-ups move to the new hours by day.
editor.allWarn: You are changing the whole series — including appointments that already took place. Usually “This and following” is right.

titlePlaceholder.mass: Name, e.g. High Mass — empty: just the time

editor.publicHint: The name is public — it stands in the plan and on the notice board. Place and note stay encrypted.
editor.privateSeen: Only you see it — encrypted with your key.
editor.reserveAsCalendar: who books: as in the calendar ({who})
editor.linkWarn: The link must start with https:// (or #/ for a page on recreatio.pl).
editor.newPartNote: Programme item: {parent} — calendar, visibility, place, link and people are shared with it. Change here only what should be different in this item.
editor.willDetach: After saving, this appointment will no longer be a programme item.
editor.partNote: Programme item: {parent} — whatever it has the same as the parent changes along with it.
editor.fromChat: From a chat — the appointment will remember which message it came from.
editor.onlyTimeNote: You are moving only this one appointment — the rest of the series stays as it was. Bookings move with it.
editor.endSeries: End the series before this day

app.noKey: Without a key in this tab, the calendar is locked — sign in again or unlock the key.
app.notPickable: You can't change this appointment together with others.
app.clickWhere: Click the day or hour where they should go.
app.mineHint: Only appointments where you must be present (e.g. masses you celebrate)

grid.focusEvents: Appointments wide, tasks at the side
grid.focusTasks: Tasks wide, appointments at the side

list.intro: A group has its calendar right away — and can have more (e.g. masses and meetings separately). Each one says how its appointments work: who sees them, how long they last and who can book them.

day.label: Day
day.says: Start for every day of the range.

mass.label: Mass
mass.says: Start for every mass of the day (from the “Hours” node).

season.label: Liturgical season
season.says: Works out the season, week, rank of the day and colour of the season.

feasts.label: Feast calendar
feasts.says: Picks the celebration of the day from the table (highest rank wins).

if.label: Condition
if.says: Checks the day, the mass or the entry — then “yes” or “no”.

set.label: Set
set.says: Sets the title, a scheme field or a variable.

slots.label: Mass times
slots.says: Says which masses there are that day (Sundays and feasts / weekdays).

record.label: Add entry
record.says: Adds a fixed entry to the mass, e.g. the intention “For the parishioners”.

skip.label: No mass
skip.says: No mass on this day (at this hour).

end.label: Create
end.says: The mass is created with what was set along the way.

record-start.label: New entry
record-start.says: Start: someone adds or accepts an entry.

wait.label: Waits
wait.says: The entry waits until the office accepts it.

refuse.label: Refuse
refuse.says: The entry cannot be added — with this message.

dateRule.christmasSunday: Sunday in the Christmas octave (or 30 December)

trace.title: title
trace.noMassNode: (no “Mass” node — the mass with what the day set)

problem.noDay: No “Day” node — the plan does not know where to start the day.
problem.dayLoop: Too many steps on the day path — is there a loop in the plan?
problem.endOnDay: “Create” on the day path — the day ends in “Mass times” or “No mass”.
problem.notOnDay: Node “{node}” does not belong on the day path.
problem.dayEnds: The day path ends at “{node}” — no “{out}” connection (no mass times).
problem.massLoop: Too many steps on the path of the {time} mass — is there a loop in the plan?
problem.notOnMass: Node “{node}” does not belong on the mass path.

rule.waits: The entry is waiting to be accepted by the office.
rule.notInRule: (node “{node}” does not belong in the rule)
rule.endsWithout: (the rule ends at “{node}” without a decision)

rank.r2: Greatest days (Christmas, Epiphany, Ascension, Pentecost; Sundays of Advent, Lent, Easter; Ash Wednesday; Holy Week; Easter octave)
rank.r3: Solemnities of the General Calendar, All Souls
rank.r4: Proper solemnities (patron, title and anniversary of the church dedication)
rank.r6: Sundays of Ordinary Time and Christmas Time
rank.r8: Proper feasts (diocesan patron, anniversary of the cathedral dedication)
rank.r9: Privileged days (17–24 Dec, Christmas octave, days of Lent)

testLabel.festive: Sunday or holy day of obligation

placeholder.title: title of the mass (from the celebration)
placeholder.sundayName: name of the Sunday, e.g. 3rd Sunday of Advent

summary.countOthers: other appointments in the week with

node.waitDefault: The office will confirm the entry.

test.rankNote: 1 is the highest rank, 13 an ordinary weekday. “< 10” means: more important than an obligatory memorial.
test.celebrationAny: there is a celebration from the feast calendar
test.betweenNote: Every year, both ends included (e.g. 17–24 December). A “to” earlier than “from” runs across New Year.
test.countWeekOcc: other appointments this week that have such entries

kind.advent: Relative to the 1st Sunday of Advent
kind.baptism: Baptism of the Lord (Sunday after 6 Jan)

season.note: The node works out the season, week and rank of the day (e.g. a Sunday of Advent) — anew every year, from the dates of Easter and Advent. You enter the colours.

slots.keyHint: Key — conditions and the preview recognise this mass by it
slots.label: Description (optional)
slots.note: On Sundays and holy days of obligation (a celebration marked “feast day”) the first list applies, on other days the second.

feasts.note: Of the celebrations falling on a day, the one with the highest rank (the smallest number) wins — if it is more important than the day itself (e.g. a Sunday of Advent has rank 2). It sets the celebration, colour and feast day.
feasts.empty: The table is empty — add the first celebration.
feasts.namePlaceholder: e.g. Solemnity of Our Lady Queen of Poland
feasts.title: Mass title (empty: name of the celebration)
feasts.festiveLong: Feast day — masses as on Sunday
feasts.move: When the day has a higher rank — celebrate on the next day

panel.colourNote: The variable “colour” is the colour of the mass: it is then written into a field (e.g. “Set field Colour = {token}”).
panel.recordNote: The entry is created together with the mass and marked “by rule” — the office can change or delete it.

messagePlaceholder.refuse: e.g. This mass already has an intention.
messagePlaceholder.wait: e.g. The office will confirm the entry.

missing.day: No “{node}” node — every day starts from it.
missing.mass: No “{node}” node — every mass starts from it.
missing.record: No “{node}” node — checking an entry starts from it.

flowEditor.tooMany: There are {count} “{node}” nodes — only one counts.
flowEditor.help: Click a node to set it up. Connect an output (dot on the right) to the input of the next node (dot on the left). A new node added next to the selected one connects to its free output. Delete removes the selected node or edge.
flowEditor.planHelp: For every day the path starts in “Day” and ends in “Mass times”; for every mass — it starts in “Mass” and ends in “Create” or “No mass”.

rule.intentionWaits: The intention is waiting to be accepted by the office.
rule.singleAlone: This mass already has an intention — a single intention must be the only one.
rule.noMixed: This mass has a single intention — a collective one cannot be added to it.
rule.weekFull: This week there are already two masses with collective intentions.
rule.noPlaces: There are no free places left.

obchod.label: Celebration
obchod.says: Celebration of the day or mass formulary (e.g. “All Saints”, “30th Sunday in Ordinary Time”) — shown in the plan and on the notice board.

kolor.label: Vestment colour
kolor.says: Colour of the liturgical vestments — shown in the plan as a colour mark.

czytania.label: Readings
czytania.says: References of the readings, e.g. “Isa 7:10-14; Ps 24; Rom 1:1-7; Matt 1:18-24” — references only, no texts.

msza.name: Mass
msza.says: Mass with celebration, vestment colour, readings and intentions (with the rule for single and collective ones).
msza.listSays: Mass intentions: the text read at mass and on the notice board; a single one stands alone, collective ones at most at two masses a week.

nabozenstwo.name: Service
nabozenstwo.says: Service (Rosary, Stations of the Cross, Lenten Lamentations …) with celebration and colour.

spowiedz.name: Confession
spowiedz.says: Confession with a short public note.
spowiedz.fieldSays: A short note in the plan, e.g. “at St Joseph’s confessional”.

zapisy.name: Meeting with sign-ups
zapisy.says: A meeting people can sign up for (e.g. confirmation candidates choose a date).
zapisy.notesSays: Notes on the sign-up — the office sees them.
zapisy.listSays: Sign-ups for a date: “I’ll come” counts towards the places (20, can be changed in the rule); a sign-up from outside awaits confirmation.

year.name: Liturgical year — parish (Poland)
year.says: Masses for the coming weeks following the liturgical year: the calendar of feasts in Poland, Sunday and weekday times, Triduum, Christmas midnight mass, the celebration and colour of each mass, a votive mass of Our Lady of Perpetual Help on Wednesday evening, and the intention “For the parishioners” on Sunday at 12:13.

fixed.name: Fixed mass times
fixed.says: Only the times: Sundays and feasts 7:30, 9:00, 10:30, 12:13, 18:00; weekdays 7:00 and 18:00 — without the calendar of feasts.
